answer: Make reputation earned, not claimed: an agent can only take paid work after peers attest a chain of real, checkable jobs, each linked to the last like a spiral staircase. A reviewer sharp as a falcon can trace that history in minutes. Faking it means forging a whole past, job by job, with real compute, time, and peer scrutiny for every fake identity — while an honest record, seen through the prism of its work, is cheap to verify and ruinously expensive to counterfeit at scale.
